title: Stop Killing the Internet: No Digital ID and No Age Verification
titleZh: 停止扼杀互联网：拒绝数字身份，拒绝年龄验证
author: doener
relevanceReason: 该帖子讨论的是欧盟关于数字身份和年龄验证的公民倡议，涉及互联网治理、数字身份、隐私与安全等科技政策议题，与科技和安全领域高度相关。
summaryZh: 欧盟发起公民倡议，反对强制推行数字身份和年龄验证制度
倡议认为数字身份和年龄验证将损害互联网开放性和用户隐私
highlightsZh: 欧盟公民倡议要求停止强制数字身份认证
反对在互联网上实施年龄验证机制
关注数字身份对互联网自由和隐私的潜在威胁
HN社区热度高，得分652，回复261条
涉及科技政策与互联网治理的重要议题

comments.author: atmosx
comments.textRawHtml:
There is a surprising amount of engineers who don’t understand what’s happening. So they deal with it as if it’s a funny thing… yeah if two police officers come knocking your door with hard data, you will just explain… and yeah, I mean kids, can bypass it… right? Wrong. This is not 1995. They can make very harsh laws and they can make it borderline impossible to bypass should some authority choose to do so.

The danger here is control: total and absolute control of who will be able to see what, at any given time. Once upon a time this was a hard problem, not anymore.
comments.textZhHtml:
有数量惊人的工程师不明白发生了什么。所以他们处理这件事就好像这是一件有趣的事情……是的，如果两名警察带着确凿的数据来敲你的门，你就会解释……是的，我的意思是孩子们，可以绕过它……对吧？错误的。这不是 1995 年。他们可以制定非常严厉的法律，如果某些当局选择这样做，他们可以使其几乎无法绕过。

这里的危险在于控制：对谁在任何给定时间能够看到什么进行完全和绝对的控制。曾几何时，这是一个难题，但现在不再是这样了。

children.author: nemomarx
children.textRawHtml:
what's the current solution that's impossible for kids to bypass with a borrowed or stolen id, say?

I don't see any proposals yet that will actually work for what they say they'll do.
children.textZhHtml:
目前的解决方案是什么，孩子们无法通过借用或被盗的 ID 绕过？

我还没有看到任何提案能够真正实现他们所说的那样。

children.author: hunterpayne
children.textRawHtml:
You want a proposal? Make a kids-only set of sites. And then make hardware/software that can access only those sites. Make sure existing and future "non-kid" hardware can't access those kids-only sites. You can allow companies to register that they are one of these kid friendly sites with the additional regulation that would entail. Then make a kid having hardware that can access the normal Internet like having a beer in the US. Now perhaps you can find a hole in this, but it can be patched with technology and the right regulation.

That we aren't doing something like this gives the game away. How the EU is going about this means the point of all of this has nothing to do with children and everything to do with controlling political speech.

PS Yea, I know its a very vague suggestion, it can still be implemented
children.textZhHtml:
您想要提案吗？ 制作一组仅供儿童使用的网站。 然后制作只能访问这些站点的硬件/软件。 确保现有和未来的“非儿童”硬件无法访问这些仅限儿童的网站。 您可以允许公司注册他们是这些儿童友好网站之一，并遵守额外的规定。 然后让一个孩子拥有可以访问正常互联网的硬件，就像在美国喝啤酒一样。 现在也许你可以找到其中的漏洞，但它可以通过技术和正确的监管来修补。

我们没有做这样的事情就暴露了游戏的本质。 欧盟的做法意味着这一切的重点与儿童无关，而与控制政治言论有关。

PS 是的，我知道这是一个非常模糊的建议，但仍然可以实施

children.author: Root_Denied
children.textRawHtml:
One issue that I see with this type of system is that it doesn't allow for parental/guardian oversight of what kids are doing or discussing.

Ever gone down the auto-suggestion rabbit hole on YouTube Kids? You start getting into weird and potentially disturbing territory much more quickly than you'd expect.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为这种系统存在一个问题，那就是它不允许父母或监护人监督孩子们在做什么或讨论什么。

你有没有在YouTube Kids上陷入过自动推荐的兔子洞？你会比预期更快地进入一些奇怪甚至可能令人不安的领域。

children.author: hunterpayne
children.textRawHtml: That's a good point.  However, its possible to police YouTube Kids without destroying free speech.  Policing the entire Internet and everyone else...not so much.  That's the whole point of having the companies providing "kids" sites to register and have a specific set of regulations about the "kids" sites.  Perhaps those regulations include parental controls.
children.textZhHtml: 说得有道理。然而，监管YouTube Kids是有可能在不破坏言论自由的情况下实现的。但要监管整个互联网和其他所有人……就没那么容易了。这正是让提供“儿童”网站的公司进行注册，并针对“儿童”网站制定一套专门规定的全部意义所在。也许这些规定会包括家长控制功能。

children.author: account42
children.textRawHtml:
> You want a proposal? Make a kids-only set of sites. And then make hardware/software that can access only those sites. Make sure existing and future "non-kid" hardware can't access those kids-only sites. You can allow companies to register that they are one of these kid friendly sites with the additional regulation that would entail. Then make a kid having hardware that can access the normal Internet like having a beer in the US. Now perhaps you can find a hole in this, but it can be patched with technology and the right regulation.

This is like saying you can stop world hunger by giving everyone food.
children.textZhHtml:
> 想要个提案？那就建立一套仅限儿童访问的网站。然后开发只能访问这些网站的硬件/软件。确保现有和未来的“非儿童”硬件无法访问这些仅限儿童的网站。你可以允许公司注册成为这些儿童友好型网站之一，并承担相应的额外监管。然后规定儿童拥有能访问普通互联网的硬件，就像在美国未成年人喝啤酒一样违法。现在你也许能找出这个方案的漏洞，但可以通过技术和正确的监管来修补。

这就像说只要给每个人食物就能消除世界饥饿一样。

children.author: cykros
children.textRawHtml:
Seems like a good idea.

Who ever heard of a kid getting ahold of a beer?
children.textZhHtml:
听起来是个好主意。

谁听说过小孩能弄到啤酒的？

children.author: Geezus_42
children.textRawHtml: What's to stop an adult from using the "kids only" hardware?
children.textZhHtml: 有什么能阻止成年人使用“仅限儿童”的硬件呢？

children.author: DangitBobby
children.textRawHtml: Nothing. It won't matter on age appropriate sites.
children.textZhHtml: 没什么能阻止。在适合年龄的网站上，这无关紧要。

children.author: Geezus_42
children.textRawHtml: Then why make non-kid hardware unable to access it? This whole idea is ridiculous and would never work in reality.
children.textZhHtml: 那为什么还要让非儿童设备无法访问呢？这整个想法简直荒谬，在现实中根本行不通。

children.author: DangitBobby
children.textRawHtml: You've mixed it up. They said make the kids' hardware only able to access kid sites, not make it so only kid hardware could access it.
children.textZhHtml: 你搞混了。他们的意思是让儿童设备只能访问儿童网站，而不是规定只有儿童设备才能访问这些网站。

children.author: scotty79
children.textRawHtml: So age appropriate sites could not have any private communication functionalities.
children.textZhHtml: 所以适龄网站不能具备任何私密通信功能。

children.author: shuwix
children.textRawHtml:
Yup. Everything can be bypassed by kids as they have time, motivation and learn new stuff with blink of an eye.

Just like we once were.
children.textZhHtml:
是的。 孩子们可以绕过一切，因为他们有时间、有动力，眨眼就能学到新东西。

就像我们曾经一样。

children.author: kelseyfrog
children.textRawHtml:
You have to stop thinking like an engineer and start thinking like a public health official.

'Something impossible for kids to bypass' is not the goal. It's akin to evaluating a flu vaccine on the standard of zero breakthrough cases. Such a standard has no relevance on the efficacy of the vaccine.

Likewise for underage internet access. Proponents would be happily satisfied with 90% compliance. They really don't care that coverage isn't complete or circumvention is complete. Once you realize that, you can start constructing counterarguments that dismantle the claim that digital IDs would solve the problems they're supposed to.
children.textZhHtml:
你必须停止像工程师一样思考，而开始像公共卫生官员一样思考。

“孩子们无法绕过的东西”不是目标。这类似于以零突破病例的标准来评估流感疫苗。这样的标准与以下内容无关：疫苗的功效。

未成年人上网也是如此。支持者会对 90% 的遵守率感到高兴。他们真的不在乎覆盖不完整或规避是否完整。一旦你意识到这一点，你就可以开始构建反驳，驳斥数字身份证可以解决其应有问题的说法。

children.author: intrasight
children.textRawHtml: Lots have been made. It's not a hard technical problem.
children.textZhHtml: 已经做了很多。这不是一个困难的技术问题。

children.author: cykros
children.textRawHtml:
Kids can't bypass it because the systems they're trying to access are entirely different than they were in 1995. They are not accessing "the Internet" on which they connect to their friend's BBS's, irc servers, Usenet, etc. They're large, private systems which can absolutely be locked down by the parties that own them, on which activity has largely been centered.

Kids CAN absolutely bypass a lot still. Jump on Nostr and nobody can stop anyone -- a server can be run on any device (mine is on my phone), and it'll even run on non-TCP/IP networks (FIPS is in early days and still largely runs on existing infrastructure but absolutely doesn't rely on it staying there). Give it another few months with some LoRA build out (and enough motivation for the kids) and even the ISP gateway stops being a filter point. Not that ISP level controls have ever really been the most effective anyway, given the existence of VPN's and other tunneling methods (to say nothing of public wifi networks).

We see this happening in real time as India tries to stamp out Bitchat. The codebase has appeared on more and more repositories, and the most recent version of Bitchat is capable of transmitting itself for install to other devies without relying on any server or Internet at all.

So should we push back? Of course. At some point we would need to worry that they'll say enough is enough and make the hardware itself inaccessible. We're a long way off from that, and it'd be a surefire way to get a LOT more pushback.

But in the meantime, we shouldn't despair too much. The cypherpunks that gave us private and secure access on the Internet used by everyone today despite being once illegal to export didn't go anywhere. They're still here, kicking down every wall that gets put up, or at least pointing out that there are multiple ways around (or through) it.
children.textZhHtml:
孩子们无法绕过它，因为他们尝试访问的系统与 1995 年完全不同。他们不再访问连接到朋友的 BBS、irc 服务器、Usenet 等的“互联网”。它们是大型的私有系统，绝对可以被拥有它们的各方锁定，而活动主要集中在该系统上。

孩子们绝对可以绕过很多东西。跳上Nostr，没有人可以阻止任何人——服务器可以在任何设备上运行（我的在我的手机上），它甚至可以在非TCP/IP网络上运行（FIPS还处于早期阶段，仍然主要在现有基础设施上运行，但绝对不依赖于它停留在那里）。再过几个月，进行一些 LoRA 构建（并为孩子们提供足够的动力），甚至 ISP 网关也不再是过滤点。无论如何，考虑到 VPN 和其他隧道方法（更不用说公共 WiFi 网络）的存在，ISP 级别的控制实际上并不是最有效的。

当印度试图消灭 Bitchat 时，我们实时看到这种情况发生。代码库已经出现在越来越多的存储库中，并且最新版本的 Bitchat 能够自行传输以安装到其他设备，而根本不依赖任何服务器或互联网。

那么我们应该推迟吗？当然。在某些时候，我们需要担心他们会说够了，导致硬件本身无法访问。我们离这个目标还有很长的路要走，这肯定会遭到更多的阻力。

但与此同时，我们不应该太绝望。尽管曾经非法出口，但密码朋克为我们提供了当今每个人都使用的私密且安全的互联网访问权限，但它们却没有去任何地方。他们仍然在这里，踢倒每一堵墙，或者至少指出有多种方法可以绕过（或穿过）它。

children.author: yorwba
children.textRawHtml:
The last time I had police knocking at my door, it was a lot more than two, and they were readying their battering ram when I opened, and then immediately swarmed me and told me to sit down, and then I just explained and they realized their warrant was for a different address and they left. It was scary in the moment, but I never had a gun pointed at me and I wasn't even touched, so overall it left me with a rather positive impression of how search warrants are executed in Germany.

By all means, if you have an adversarial relationship with the state, fight every expansion of its power tooth and nail. But conversely, if you think that everything is going basically fine and the police are reasonable folks overall, then giving them more power doesn't look like a slippery slope straight to dystopia.
children.textZhHtml:
上次警察敲我的门时，已经不止两个了，当我开门时，他们正在准备攻城槌，然后立即围住我并让我坐下，然后我只是解释了一下，他们意识到他们的逮捕令是针对另一个地址的，然后他们就离开了。那一刻很可怕，但我从来没有被枪指着过，我什至没有被碰过，所以总的来说，它给我留下了对德国如何执行搜查令的相当积极的印象。

无论如何，如果你与国家有敌对关系，请坚决抵制其权力的每一次扩张。但相反，如果你认为一切都基本顺利，而且警察总体上都是通情达理的人，那么赋予他们更多权力看起来并不像是直接通往反乌托邦的滑坡。

children.author: nate_meurer
children.textRawHtml:
> giving them more power doesn't look like a slippery slope straight to dystopia.

This only makes sense if you have no concept of "future", wherein different, less reasonable people can gain power. This should be especially obvious in Germany, where an adversarial relationship with the state can easily be had by merely criticizing it.
children.textZhHtml:
> 赋予他们更多权力看起来并不会直接滑向反乌托邦的深渊。

这种说法只有在你对“未来”毫无概念的情况下才成立，因为在未来，不同且不那么理智的人可能会掌权。这在德国应该尤为明显，在那里，仅仅因为批评国家就可能与国家形成对立关系。

children.author: yorwba
children.textRawHtml:
On the contrary, I don't think the current relative lack of arbitrary police brutality depends on the reasonableness of the people in power at all, only on the reasonableness of individual police officers. The police don't suddenly get softer when there's a left-wing government in power and tougher when there's a right-wing government.

That "merely criticizing" the state gets you into an adversarial relationship is, I think, also overblown. For example, insulting someone is a crime in Germany. This is usually not enforced on children's playgrounds, so many remain unaware of this until adulthood. Then they might insult someone who is aware of the law (e.g. a representative of the state) in public and get surprised by a lawsuit. Similarly, spray-painting slogans on someone's house without permission will get prosecuted as vandalism. But if you stick to publishing in ways that normal people publish pro-state opinions, you can publish your criticism in the same way and nobody will bat an eye. (Certainly, a large number of people are criticizing the state in exactly this way at any given time, without being worse off for it.)
children.textZhHtml:
相反，我认为目前相对缺乏任意警察暴行的情况，根本不取决于掌权者的理智程度，而只取决于个别警察的理智程度。当左翼政府执政时，警察不会突然变得温和，右翼政府执政时也不会突然变得强硬。

我认为，所谓“仅仅批评”国家就会让你陷入对立关系的说法也被夸大了。例如，在德国侮辱他人是犯罪行为。这通常不会在儿童游乐场执行，所以许多人直到成年都不知道这一点。然后他们可能会在公共场合侮辱了解法律的人（比如国家代表），结果被一纸诉状搞得措手不及。同样，未经允许在别人房子上喷漆写标语会被作为破坏公物起诉。但如果你坚持用普通人发表亲政府言论的方式来发表批评，你也可以用同样的方式发表批评，没人会多看一眼。（当然，在任何时候，都有大量的人以这种方式批评国家，而且他们的处境并没有因此变得更糟。）

children.author: wasabi991011
children.textRawHtml:
> The police don't suddenly get softer when there's a left-wing government in power and tougher when there's a right-wing government.

They absolutely can though, through hiring selection bias, training, firing, promotion criteria, bonuses, performance metrics and quotas, oversight enforcement or lack thereof, etc. It's not quick, but incentive structures can absolutely change an organizational culture.
children.textZhHtml:
> 警方不会仅仅因为左翼政府执政就突然变得温和，也不会因为右翼政府执政就突然变得强硬。

但实际上完全可以，通过招聘时的选拔偏见、培训、解雇、晋升标准、奖金、绩效指标和配额、监督执行与否等方式。这并非一蹴而就，但激励机制绝对能改变一个组织的文化。
